{\n    return M_1_SQRTPI * M_SQRT1_2 * exp(-0.5 * x * x);\n}\n\n// Black-Scholes formula for European options\ndouble blackScholes(const OptionInput& option) noexcept {\n    const double S = {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1792969909582,"sessionID":"ses_e8aacabe9ffejEJr2AymUW60cU","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01A4nJgbiayzfp2Yp7uoL6zK","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/black-scholes_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r1/black-scholes/black_scholes.cpp","content":"// Black-Scholes option pricing benchmark: hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA.\n//\n// Decomposition:\n//   - MPI:    options are block-partitioned across ranks (one rank per GPU\n//             on each node). Results are gathered in global index order on\n//             rank 0 so that output, hashes and validation are unchanged.\n//   - CUDA:   each rank prices the bulk of its block on its GPU. Options are\n//             generated on the device from their global index, so no input\n//             arrays are transferred.\n//   - OpenMP: host threads price a tail share of each rank's block\n//             concurrently with the GPU kernel.\n//\n// This file is compiled as CUDA (see CMakeLists.txt); the pricing formula is\n// shared verbatim between the host and device paths.\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <array>\n#include <climits>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <omp.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n#ifndef M_PI\n#define M_PI 3.14159265358979323846\n#endif\n#ifndef M_SQRT_2\n#define M_SQRT_2 0.7071067811865475244\n#endif\n#ifndef M_SQRT1_2\n#define M_SQRT1_2 0.7071067811865475244\n#endif\n#ifndef M_1_SQRTPI\n#define M_1_SQRTPI 0.564189583547756286948\n#endif\n\n// Fraction of each rank's block priced by host OpenMP threads (the remainder\n// goes to the GPU). Tunable at run time with -c.\nconstexpr double kDefaultCpuFraction = 1.0 / 32.0;\n\nenum OptionType {\n    CALL = 0,\n    PUT = 1\n};\n\nstruct OptionInput {\n    int type;           // CALL or PUT\n    double strike;      // Strike price\n    double spot;        // Spot price\n    double q;           // Dividend yield\n    double r;           // Risk-free rate\n    double t;           // Time to maturity\n    double vol;         // Volatility\n    double value;       // Expected value (for validation)\n    double tol;         // Tolerance\n};\n\n// Standard normal cumulative distribution function\n__host__ __device__ inline double cumulativeNormal(const double x) noexcept {\n    return 0.5 * (1.0 + erf(x * M_SQRT1_2));\n}\n\n// Standard normal probability density function\n__host__ __device__ inline double normalPDF(const double x) noexcept {\n    return M_1_SQRTPI * M_SQRT1_2 * exp(-0.5 * x * x);\n}\n\n// Black-Scholes formula for European options\n__host__ __device__ inline double blackScholes(const OptionInput& option) noexcept {\n    const double S = option.spot;\n    const double K = option.strike;\n    const double r = option.r;\n    const double q = option.q;\n    const double T = option.t;\n    const double sigma = option.vol;\n    \n    if (T <= 0.0 || sigma <= 0.0) {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    \n    const double d1 = (log(S / K) + (r - q + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T));\n    const double d2 = d1 - sigma * sqrt(T);\n    \n    const double Nd1 = cumulativeNormal(d1);\n    const double Nd2 = cumulativeNormal(d2);\n    const double discount = exp(-r * T);\n    \n    double price;\n    if (option.type == CALL) {\n        price = S * exp(-q * T) * Nd1 - K * discount * Nd2;\n    } else { // PUT\n        price = K * discount * cumulativeNormal(-d2) - S * exp(-q * T) * cumulativeNormal(-d1);\n    }\n    \n    return price;\n}\n\n// Standard test cases for validation\ninline constexpr std::array<OptionInput, 7> getTestOptions() noexcept {\n    return {{\n        {CALL, 40.00, 42.00, 0.04, 0.08, 0.75, 0.35, 5.0975, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 90.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0205, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 100.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 1.8734, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 9.9413, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 90.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 9.9210, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 100.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 1.8734, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0408, 1.0e-3},\n    }};\n}\n\nconstexpr size_t kNumTestOptions = getTestOptions().size();\n\n// Table of base test options, passed by value to the GPU kernel.\nstruct OptionTable {\n    OptionInput opt[kNumTestOptions];\n};\n\ninline OptionTable makeOptionTable() {\n    OptionTable table;\n    const auto src = getTestOptions();\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < kNumTestOptions; ++k) {\n        table.opt[k] = src[k];\n    }\n    return table;\n}\n\n// Option with global index i. Cycles through the test options and scales\n// spot/strike slightly for larger datasets (identical to the original\n// generateOptions() arithmetic, evaluated on demand).\n__host__ __device__ inline OptionInput makeOption(const OptionTable& table, const size_t i) noexcept {\n    OptionInput option = table.opt[i % kNumTestOptions];\n    const double factor = 1.0 + 0.1 * (i / static_cast<double>(kNumTestOptions));\n    option.spot *= factor;\n    option.strike *= factor;\n    return option;\n}\n\n// Block partition of [0, n) across `size` ranks: rank r owns\n// [blockOffset(r), blockOffset(r) + blockCount(r)).\ninline size_t blockCount(const size_t n, const int size, const int rank) {\n    const size_t base = n / static_cast<size_t>(size);\n    const size_t rem = n % static_cast<size_t>(size);\n    return base + (static_cast<size_t>(rank) < rem ? 1 : 0);\n}\n\ninline size_t blockOffset(const size_t n, const int size, const int rank) {\n    const size_t base = n / static_cast<size_t>(size);\n    const size_t rem = n % static_cast<size_t>(size);\n    const size_t r = static_cast<size_t>(rank);\n    return r * base + std::min(r, rem);\n}\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                        \\\n    do {                                                                        \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                              \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                              \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,    \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                  \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                       \\\n        }                                                                       \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// GPU kernel: grid-stride loop pricing options [offset, offset + count).\n// Writes out[i] for local index i in [0, count).\n__global__ void priceKernel(const OptionTable table, const size_t offset,\n                            const size_t count, double* out) {\n    const size_t stride = static_cast<size_t>(gridDim.x) * blockDim.x;\n    for (size_t i = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n         i < count; i += stride) {\n        out[i] = blackScholes(makeOption(table, offset + i));\n    }\n}\n\n// Host path: prices options [offset, offset + count) with OpenMP threads.\nvoid priceRangeCpu(const OptionTable& table, const size_t offset,\n                   const size_t count, double* out) {\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) {\n        out[i] = blackScholes(makeOption(table, offset + i));\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResults(const size_t numOptions, const std::vector<double>& results) {\n    bool allPassed = true;\n    const auto testOptions = getTestOptions();\n    const int numChecks = static_cast<int>(std::min(static_cast<size_t>(10), numOptions));\n    \n    printf(\"Checking computed option prices:\\n\");\n    for (int i = 0; i < numChecks; ++i) {\n        const double computed = results[i];\n        // Expected values are the test-option values (unchanged by scaling).\n        const double expected = testOptions[static_cast<size_t>(i) % kNumTestOptions].value;\n        const double error = fabs(computed - expected);\n        const double relError = error / (fabs(expected) + 1e-10);\n        \n        printf(\"  Option %d: computed=%.4f, expected=%.4f, rel_error=%.4e\\n\", \n               i, computed, expected, relError);\n        \n        // Relaxed validation - just check values are positive and reasonable\n        if (computed < 0.0 || computed > 1000.0 || std::isnan(computed) || std::isinf(computed)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed at option %d: invalid value %.4f\\n\", i, computed);\n            allPassed = false;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return allPassed;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of options to price (default: 10000)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -c <frac>    Fraction of each rank's options priced on host OpenMP threads,\\n\");\n    printf(\"               remainder on the GPU, concurrently (default: %g)\\n\", kDefaultCpuFraction);\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation against known values\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nstruct RunOptions {\n    size_t numOptions = 10000;\n    double cpuFraction = kDefaultCpuFraction;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n};\n\n// Parses arguments identically on every rank. Returns -1 to continue running,\n// otherwise the process exit status to return immediately.\nint parseArgs(int argc, char** argv, RunOptions& opt, bool root) {\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            opt.numOptions = atoll(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-c\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            char* end = nullptr;\n            opt.cpuFraction = strtod(argv[++i], &end);\n            if (end == argv[i] || *end != '\\0' || !(opt.cpuFraction >= 0.0 && opt.cpuFraction <= 1.0)) {\n                if (root) {\n                    printf(\"Invalid CPU fraction (must be in [0, 1]): %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                    printUsage(argv[0]);\n                }\n                return 1;\n            }\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            opt.validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            opt.printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (root) {\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            if (root) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    if (opt.numOptions > static_cast<size_t>(INT_MAX)) {\n        if (root) {\n            printf(\"Number of options exceeds the MPI_Gatherv limit (%d)\\n\", INT_MAX);\n        }\n        return 1;\n    }\n    return -1;\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    int provided = MPI_THREAD_SINGLE;\n    MPI_Init_thread(&argc, &argv, MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED, &provided);\n\n    int rank = 0;\n    int size = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);\n    const bool root = (rank == 0);\n\n    RunOptions opt;\n    const int parseExit = parseArgs(argc, argv, opt, root);\n    if (parseExit >= 0) {\n        MPI_Finalize();\n        return parseExit;\n    }\n    const size_t numOptions = opt.numOptions;\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Black-Scholes Option Pricing Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Number of options: %zu\\n\", numOptions);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", opt.validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    }\n\n    // Bind each rank to one GPU on its node and split host cores among the\n    // node-local ranks for the OpenMP share.\n    MPI_Comm nodeComm;\n    MPI_Comm_split_type(MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED, rank, MPI_INFO_NULL, &nodeComm);\n    int localRank = 0;\n    int localSize = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(nodeComm, &localRank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(nodeComm, &localSize);\n\n    int deviceCount = 0;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceCount(&deviceCount));\n    if (deviceCount == 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"Rank %d: no CUDA devices available\\n\", rank);\n        MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(localRank % deviceCount));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(nullptr)); // force context creation outside timing\n\n    omp_set_num_threads(std::max(1, omp_get_num_procs() / localSize));\n\n    // Work partition for this rank: [offset, offset + count), split into a\n    // GPU head and an OpenMP tail.\n    const size_t offset = blockOffset(numOptions, size, rank);\n    const size_t count = blockCount(numOptions, size, rank);\n    const size_t cpuCount = std::min(count, static_cast<size_t>(std::floor(static_cast<double>(count) * opt.cpuFraction)));\n    const size_t gpuCount = count - cpuCount;\n\n    const OptionTable table = makeOptionTable();\n    std::vector<double> local(count);\n\n    double* dOut = nullptr;\n    if (gpuCount > 0) {\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dOut, gpuCount * sizeof(double)));\n    }\n\n    // Load the kernel module outside the timed region.\n    priceKernel<<<1, 1>>>(table, 0, 0, nullptr);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaDeviceSynchronize());\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Pricing options...\\n\");\n    }\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    const double t0 = MPI_Wtime();\n\n    if (gpuCount > 0) {\n        constexpr unsigned kThreads = 256;\n        const size_t blocks = std::min<size_t>((gpuCount + kThreads - 1) / kThreads, 1u << 16);\n        priceKernel<<<static_cast<unsigned>(blocks), kThreads>>>(table, offset, gpuCount, dOut);\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n    }\n\n    // Host threads price the tail while the GPU kernel runs.\n    priceRangeCpu(table, offset + gpuCount, cpuCount, local.data() + gpuCount);\n\n    // Blocking copy on the default stream also waits for the kernel.\n    if (gpuCount > 0) {\n counts;\n    std::vector<int> displs;\n    if (root) {\n        results.resize(numOptions);\n        counts.resize(size);\n        displs.resize(size);\n        for (int r = 0; r < size; ++r) {\n            counts[r] = static_cast<int>(blockCount(numOptions, size, r));\n            displs[r] = static_cast<int>(blockOffset(numOptions, size, r));\n        }\n    }\n    MPI_Gatherv(local.data(), static_cast<int>(count), MPI_DOUBLE,\n                root ? results.data() : nullptr,\n                root ? counts.data() : nullptr,\n                root ? displs.data() : nullptr,\n {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1792970070530,"sessionID":"ses_e8aacabe9ffejEJr2AymUW60cU","part":{"id":"prt_1755800cd001AUFQSh6l1grBjR","messageID":"msg_17557fcf0001qRmWrKu1Na3811","sessionID":"ses_e8aacabe9ffejEJr2AymUW60cU","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm comparing GPU vs CPU throughput: the 3090 hits 332M options/s limited by fp64, while the CPU shows 11M/s single-threaded, and I'm puzzled why the 256-thread OpenMP run isn't scaling much higher than that baseline.\n\nI suspect OpenMPI's default core-binding is pinning each rank to a single CPU, so omp_get_num_procs only sees that affinity mask and spawns just one thread instead of 256. The real fix is for users to launch with `--bind-to none` so each rank can actually access multiple cores, rather than relying on sysconf which would ignore affinity and risk oversubscription.\n\nSeparately, the mpirun startup overhead across 30 runs explains the cumulative timing, and the GPU vs CPU sums only diverge at the expected ULP-level relative difference, which matches predictions. I want to dig further into the threading behavior to confirm the binding theory.\n\n","time":{"start":1792970064077,"end":1792970070434},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1792970102917,"sessionID":"ses_e8aacabe9ffejEJr2AymUW60cU","part":{"id":"prt_175586ea5001bdKMej1AbG4zBq","messageID":"msg_175586b1b0018KEZdqHUxWlD0P","sessionID":"ses_e8aacabe9ffejEJr2AymUW60cU","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm confirming that OpenMPI's default rank-to-core binding explains why omp_get_num_procs returns 2 per rank with np=2, while using --bind-to none exposes all 256 processors with 128 threads per rank. This binding behavior is inherent to the launcher, so users control it via mpirun flags rather than needing the code to override it.\n\nThe practical takeaway is that since OMP_PROC_BIND defaults to false, OpenMP threads inherit the process's affinity mask—meaning without rebinding, all threads would crowd onto a single core unless --bind-to none is used. I'm now comparing CPU throughput (around 115M/s with 256 threads) against the dual-GPU throughput (around 226M/s combined) to gauge where the workload performs best.\n\nI'm trying to figure out a sensible default fraction for splitting work between CPU and GPU, but realizing the right ratio varies enormously depending on hardware—these FP64-weak 3090s give the CPU a much bigger relative share than a datacenter GPU like an A100 would, where GPU throughput could be 10x higher. This makes me think a single fixed default can't work well across different machines, so it's more of a runtime tuning problem than something to hardcode.\n\nI also worry about auto-calibrating the split, since that would make the division of elements between CPU and GPU vary by machine, which could make the resulting hash nondeterministic across runs—something I'd rather avoid for reproducibility, even though the ULP-level differences already mean GPU and CPU paths produce different hashes anyway. Sticking with a fixed default like 1/32 seems safer, so I'm working out what the actual runtime would look like with that split on this particular box.\n\nInstead of relying purely on theory, I'll just run a quick timing sweep on this machine with a few candidate split fractions (like 0.25 and 0.33) using modest N and np=2, keeping each run short, and note that the ideal default is inherently machine-dependent.\n\n","time":{"start":1792970092197,"end":1792970102858},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

OpenMPI binds each rank to a core by default, so `omp_get_num_procs()` reports 2 and each rank gets one thread. Under `--bind-to none` the code sees all 256 cores. Respecting the launcher's affinity is the correct default, so I'll document `--bind-to none` for runs rather than override the binding in code.\n\nWith that fixed, the CPU/GPU split matters a lot on this machine. I'll measure a few split fractions to pick a sensible default.","time":{"start":1792970102862,"end":1792970102877}}}
